title: [Docs] CHANGELOG has no entry for about 100 commits after 2026-11-03 and still says HTTP/2 through CONNECT and over SslStream works today
body:
## Summary
CHANGELOG.md has only the [1.0.0-pre.1] section dated 2026-11-02. About 100 commits have landed since, including user-visible changes (opt-in HTTP/2 in CONNECT tunnels, Http2Options.MaxConnectionsPerOrigin, UHttpClient.DisposeAsync), and lines 16-17 and 44-45 contradict the code. Readers and the release-notes script get stale information.

## Location
- `CHANGELOG.md:16`

## Problem
The only section is [1.0.0-pre.1] - 2026-11-02 (CHANGELOG.md:8); the file was last touched 2026-11-03 (git log), while 100 commits landed since, several user-visible: HTTP/2 in CONNECT tunnels made opt-in (#382), Http2Options.MaxConnectionsPerOrigin and ReuseProbeIdleThreshold (#396), UHttpClient.DisposeAsync (#385), WebSocket DisposeAsync sending Close (#390), LiteJson strictness (#395), 417 handling (#392). Lines 16-17 and 44-45 still say HTTP/2 through a CONNECT tunnel 'is negotiated today' and 'must ship off by default'; Http2Options.EnableHttp2ThroughConnectTunnels now defaults to false (Runtime/Core/Http2Options.cs:19). Lines 28-29 describe TurboHTTP.Transport as 'HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over SslStream', which PlatformNotes.md:55-60 says cannot happen on Unity. The assembly list omits TurboHTTP.UniTask.WebSocket. Background networking cites #265 (:19, :49) where PlatformNotes cites #266.

**Failure scenario.** A user reading the changelog to decide whether proxy deployments get HTTP/2, or what changed since the commit they pinned, gets the opposite of current behaviour and no record of new options or changed dispose semantics.

## Suggested fix
Add an [Unreleased] section maintained per PR (the release notes script already reads the file), correct the CONNECT and SslStream statements, and make check_repo fail when Runtime public behaviour changes without a changelog line if that discipline is wanted before the API freeze.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CHANGELOG.md has an [Unreleased] section listing the user-visible changes since 2026-11-03 (HTTP/2 CONNECT opt-in, Http2Options additions, UHttpClient.DisposeAsync, WebSocket DisposeAsync, LiteJson strictness, 417 handling).
- [ ] The statements about HTTP/2 through a CONNECT tunnel and HTTP/2 over SslStream match the current code.
- [ ] The release-notes script still parses the file; the per-PR changelog discipline is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md or the PR template.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `docs-accuracy-11` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/docs.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: docs.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: CHANGELOG.md has one section, [1.0.0-pre.1] - 2026-11-02 (:8), last touched 2026-11-03 in 466935d; 'git log 466935d..HEAD' counts 75 commits, not about 100. The user-visible ones named in the finding are there (#382, #385, #390, #392, #395, #396). Lines 16-17 and 44-45 say HTTP/2 through CONNECT 'is negotiated today' and 'must ship off by default'; the field _enableHttp2ThroughConnectTunnels has no initialiser, so it defaults to false (Runtime/Core/Http2Options.cs:19) since #382. Line 28-29 describes Transport as 'HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 over SslStream', which PlatformNotes.md:53-58 says never happens on Unity. Runtime/UniTask.WebSocket exists and is missing from the assembly list. #265 is the merged background-networking PR and #266 the open device-validation issue, so the #265 citation for 'validation pending' points at the wrong number. Low: the section describes a version that was never tagged, and release-checklist.md:71-73 treats [Unreleased] as optional, but Tools~/ci/release_notes.py would publish these statements as the release notes when the tag is cut. #101 lists 'CHANGELOG discipline' in general; it does not track these statements.

title: [Docs] APIReference describes WithHeaders(headers) as 'Set several headers' but it replaces every header, including the client's DefaultHeaders
body:
## Summary
UHttpRequest.WithHeaders clears the header collection and copies the argument, so default headers applied in CreateRequest are lost. The reference table says it sets several headers, which suggests an additive call. Users calling it lose Accept, Authorization or other defaults silently.

## Location
- `Documentation~/APIReference.md:79`

## Problem
UHttpRequest.WithHeaders clears the header collection and copies the argument (Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs:192-202); default headers were applied earlier in CreateRequest (UHttpClient.cs:182). The XML summary says 'Replaces all headers'.

**Failure scenario.** client.Get(url).WithHeader('Accept', 'application/json').WithHeaders(extra) silently drops Accept and default headers such as an API key or User-Agent set in DefaultHeaders.

## Suggested fix
Correct the table row, and consider an additive AddHeaders or a clearer name for the replacing overload.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Documentation~/APIReference.md states that WithHeaders replaces all headers, including those from DefaultHeaders, and points to the additive alternative (WithHeader).
- [ ] The wording matches the XML summary 'Replaces all headers' in Runtime/Core/UHttpRequest.cs.
- [ ] Optional: a decision is recorded on adding an additive AddHeaders overload or renaming; any API change gets XML docs and a test in Tests/Runtime/Core/.

title: [Docs] APIReference says GetBodyAsString() honours the content type charset; it always decodes UTF-8 and returns null for an empty body
body:
## Summary
UHttpResponse.GetBodyAsString() decodes with Encoding.UTF8 unconditionally and returns null when the body is empty. The reference says UTF-8 'unless the content type says otherwise' and does not list GetContentEncoding(), the real way to get the charset. Callers on non-UTF-8 responses get mojibake and callers on empty bodies get an unexpected null.

## Location
- `Documentation~/APIReference.md:113`

## Problem
UHttpResponse.GetBodyAsString() decodes with Encoding.UTF8 unconditionally and returns null when the body is empty (Runtime/Core/UHttpResponse.cs:153-164); the charset is only available through the separate GetContentEncoding() (:189-229), which the reference does not list.

**Failure scenario.** A response with Content-Type: text/plain; charset=ISO-8859-1 is decoded as UTF-8 and non-ASCII characters become U+FFFD; response.GetBodyAsString().Length on a 204 throws NullReferenceException.

## Suggested fix
Fix the table row, list GetContentEncoding() and GetBodyAsString(response.GetContentEncoding()), and state the null result (or return an empty string).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] APIReference.md states that GetBodyAsString() always uses UTF-8 and returns null for an empty body.
- [ ] APIReference.md lists GetContentEncoding() and shows GetBodyAsString(response.GetContentEncoding()).
- [ ] Documented behaviour is pinned by a NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Core/ covering a non-UTF-8 charset and an empty body.

## Context

title: [Docs] Streaming response Body is documented as a plain read-only Stream, but its synchronous Read blocks on the async read with no timeout
body:
## Summary
ResponseBodyStream.Read calls ReadCoreAsync(..., CancellationToken.None).GetAwaiter().GetResult(), which is sync-over-async with no deadline. APIReference.md says only 'A read-only Stream over the body' and nothing warns against StreamReader.ReadToEnd or CopyTo. Callers on the Unity main thread can hang or deadlock.

## Location
- `Documentation~/APIReference.md:125`

## Problem
APIReference.md:125 'Body: A read-only Stream over the body'. ResponseBodyStream.Read calls ReadCoreAsync(..., CancellationToken.None).GetAwaiter().GetResult() (Runtime/Core/ResponseBodyStream.cs:58-65), which is sync-over-async on a ValueTask and has no deadline (see docs-accuracy-08). Core.md:98-109 shows only ReadAsync but nothing says synchronous reads, StreamReader.ReadToEnd or CopyTo must be avoided.

**Failure scenario.** new StreamReader(streaming.Body).ReadToEnd() on the Unity main thread freezes the frame loop for the whole download, indefinitely on a stalled connection.

## Suggested fix
State in APIReference.md and the XML docs that the body must be read with ReadAsync/CopyToAsync; the Core owners should decide whether synchronous Read throws NotSupportedException instead.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] APIReference.md and the XML docs of ResponseBodyStream state that the body must be read with ReadAsync/CopyToAsync and that synchronous reads block without a deadline.
- [ ] A decision is recorded whether synchronous Read throws NotSupportedException; if changed, the behaviour is covered by a test in Tests/Runtime/Core/.
- [ ] Examples in Documentation~/ use only asynchronous reads.

title: [Docs] UHttpErrorType.Cancelled is documented as 'Cancelled by the caller' but the runtime never produces it; cancellation is OperationCanceledException
body:
## Summary
UHttpClient rethrows OperationCanceledException, and the only uses of UHttpErrorType.Cancelled are the IsRetryable switch and test transports. The APIReference error table and the enum XML doc still describe it as a live error, and the NetworkError and CertificateError summaries are narrower than their real use. Callers will write catch blocks that never fire.

## Location
- `Documentation~/APIReference.md:271`

## Problem
The only runtime references to UHttpErrorType.Cancelled are the IsRetryable switch (Runtime/Core/UHttpError.cs:85) and checks in the test transports (Runtime/Testing/MockTransport.cs:259, RecordReplayTransport.cs:521). UHttpClient rethrows OperationCanceledException (UHttpClient.cs:422-428) and Core.md:115 says so. The enum XML doc (UHttpError.cs:23) repeats the wrong meaning; the NetworkError and CertificateError summaries (:11, :20) are also narrower than their use (body-size cap, any TLS authentication failure).

**Failure scenario.** A caller following the reference writes catch (UHttpException ex) when (ex.HttpError.Type == UHttpErrorType.Cancelled) to ignore user cancellation; the handler never runs and the OperationCanceledException escapes, typically from async void.

## Suggested fix
Mark Cancelled as reserved/unused (or obsolete it) in the table and XML docs and point to OperationCanceledException; align the other two summaries with APIReference.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] APIReference.md and the XML doc in Runtime/Core/UHttpError.cs mark Cancelled as reserved/unused (or it is marked obsolete) and point to OperationCanceledException.
- [ ] The NetworkError and CertificateError summaries cover their actual uses (e.g. body-size cap, any TLS authentication failure).
- [ ] Text in APIReference.md and UHttpError.cs agrees; if the enum is obsoleted, a test in Tests/Runtime/Core/ covers the retryable classification.

title: [Docs] The documented IHttpPlugin example declares PluginCapabilities.None then calls RegisterInterceptor, which throws
body:
## Summary
The APIReference CustomLoggerPlugin example returns PluginCapabilities.None and calls context.RegisterInterceptor in InitializeAsync. PluginContext.RegisterInterceptor throws PluginException for a plugin without interceptor capabilities, and RegisterPluginAsync reports it as an initialization failure. Anyone copying the example gets an exception.

## Location
- `Documentation~/APIReference.md:350`

## Problem
APIReference.md:346-359: CustomLoggerPlugin has 'Capabilities => PluginCapabilities.None' and InitializeAsync calls context.RegisterInterceptor(new LoggingInterceptor(...)). PluginContext.RegisterInterceptor (Runtime/Core/PluginContext.cs:50-62) throws PluginException 'Plugin does not have interceptor capabilities.' unless ObserveRequests, ReadOnlyMonitoring, MutateRequests, MutateResponses or HandleErrors is set; UHttpClient.RegisterPluginAsync wraps it as 'failed during initialization' (UHttpClient.cs:252-259). The block is a declaration snippet, so Tools~/ci/doc_snippets.py compiles it, which is why CI passes. No customer doc explains PluginCapabilities.

**Failure scenario.** A user copies the Plugins example and calls client.RegisterPluginAsync(new CustomLoggerPlugin()): it always throws PluginException and no interceptor is registered.

## Suggested fix
Give the example the capability it needs (ObserveRequests for a logging interceptor), document what each PluginCapabilities flag allows, and add a runtime test that registers the documented plugin.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The example declares the capability it needs (ObserveRequests for a logging interceptor) and runs without error.
- [ ] APIReference.md documents what each PluginCapabilities flag allows.
- [ ] A NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Core/ registers the documented plugin and fails with the old example.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `docs-accuracy-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/docs.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: docs.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Documentation~/APIReference.md:346-359 declares Capabilities => PluginCapabilities.None (value 0, Runtime/Core/IHttpPlugin.cs:23) and calls context.RegisterInterceptor in InitializeAsync. PluginContext.RegisterInterceptor throws PluginException 'Plugin does not have interceptor capabilities.' when none of ObserveRequests, ReadOnlyMonitoring, MutateRequests, MutateResponses, HandleErrors is set (Runtime/Core/PluginContext.cs:50-62); RegisterPluginAsync passes plugin.Capabilities unchanged and wraps the throw as 'failed during initialization' (Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:236-259). No path relaxes the check, so the documented example always fails at registration. PluginCapabilities appears nowhere else in Documentation~, README or Samples~. The snippet only compiles in CI, which is why it passes.

title: [Docs] QuickStart and MigrationGuide do not say a default client follows no redirects, sends no Accept-Encoding and keeps no cookies
body:
## Summary
new UHttpClient() has an empty interceptor list, so 3xx responses are returned as is, no Accept-Encoding is sent and no cookies are kept, while FollowRedirects defaults to true and every QuickStart example logs the one-time 'no RedirectInterceptor' warning. MigrationGuide lists four differences from UnityWebRequest without these, and says 'No Coroutines' wrongly. Migrating users see behaviour they did not expect.

## Location
- `Documentation~/MigrationGuide.md:30`

## Problem
new UHttpClient() has an empty interceptor list: 3xx responses are returned as is (UHttpClient.cs:146-161), Accept-Encoding and decoding exist only in DecompressionInterceptor (Runtime/Middleware/DecompressionInterceptor.cs:68-71), cookies only in CookieInterceptor. FollowRedirects defaults to true, so every QuickStart example and samples 01-04 trigger the one-time warning 'FollowRedirects is true but no RedirectInterceptor is configured'. MigrationGuide.md:30-34 lists four key differences from UnityWebRequest and none of these, although UnityWebRequest follows redirects and decodes gzip by default. :31 says 'No Coroutines' while Unity.md:59-80 documents SendCoroutine/GetJsonCoroutine. README.md:143 mentions interceptors but not decompression.

**Failure scenario.** A project ported from UnityWebRequest with the guide's one-line replacement gets 301/302 responses back with IsSuccessStatusCode false for URLs that used to work, larger uncompressed downloads, lost session cookies, and a console warning from the documented setup.

## Suggested fix
Add a 'behaviour differences' section to MigrationGuide.md and a recommended-interceptors snippet (Redirect, Cookie, Decompression) to QuickStart.md, fix the coroutine line, and either make the QuickStart client configuration warning-free or explain the warning.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] MigrationGuide.md has a behaviour-differences section covering redirects, content decoding and cookies for a default client.
- [ ] QuickStart.md shows a recommended-interceptors snippet (Redirect, Cookie, Decompression) or explains the warning, and the QuickStart configuration produces no warning.
- [ ] The 'No Coroutines' line is corrected and snippets compile in the doc-snippet check.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `docs-accuracy-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/docs.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: docs.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: The code is as described: a default client has no interceptors, FollowRedirects defaults to true (Runtime/Core/UHttpClientOptions.cs:98) and the constructor logs the one-time warning (Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:146-161). QuickStart.md mentions interceptors only as a link (:175) and MigrationGuide.md:30-34 lists none of redirects, decompression or cookies; :31 says 'No Coroutines' while Unity.md:59-70 documents SendCoroutine/GetJsonCoroutine. Lowered to low because the behaviour is documented elsewhere in the customer docs: Interceptors.md:79-84 (a 3xx is returned without RedirectInterceptor), APIReference.md:144 ('applied only when a RedirectInterceptor is configured'), README.md:143, and the warning text itself names the fix. The gap is confined to the two entry documents.

title: [Docs] Docs say disposing UHttpClient releases the connection pool and sockets; a default client shares the process-wide transport and releases nothing
body:
## Summary
With default TlsBackend, ConnectionPool, Http2 and Streaming options the client uses HttpTransportFactory.Default and does not own it, so Dispose closes no connection and cancels no in-flight request. Core.md, MigrationGuide.md and APIReference.md all say Dispose frees the pool and sockets. Users rely on it for cleanup that does not happen.

## Location
- `Documentation~/Modules/Core.md:26`

## Problem
Core.md:26 'to release the connection pool and other resources it owns', MigrationGuide.md:63 'call client.Dispose() ... to free up sockets', APIReference.md:67 'release ... the connection pool'. With default TlsBackend, ConnectionPool, Http2 and Streaming options the client takes HttpTransportFactory.Default and does not own it (UHttpClient.cs:137-141, 595-605), so Dispose closes no connection and does not cancel in-flight requests; idle sockets stay until the pool's idle timeout. Only clients with a non-default option or DisposeTransport own a pool. No doc says how to close the shared pool.

**Failure scenario.** An app disposes its client on pause or scene unload expecting sockets to close and pending requests to stop; connections stay open for up to 120 s (45 s on mobile) and callbacks of in-flight requests still run on destroyed objects.

## Suggested fix
Describe the shared default transport and what Dispose does in each case, and document cancellation tokens as the way to stop in-flight requests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Core.md, MigrationGuide.md and APIReference.md describe the shared default transport and what Dispose does with an owned versus a shared transport (DisposeTransport).
- [ ] The docs name cancellation tokens as the way to stop in-flight requests.
- [ ] Statements match UHttpClient.cs behaviour; a NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Core/ pins that disposing a default client leaves the shared transport open.

## Context

title: [Docs] A leading-slash path replaces the path of BaseUrl (https://host/api + /users gives https://host/users) and the docs do not say so
body:
## Summary
ResolveUri calls new Uri(baseUri, url), which follows RFC 3986 reference resolution, so '/users' against https://host/api/ yields https://host/users while 'users' yields https://host/api/users. Docs say only 'resolved against' BaseUrl and every example uses a host-only BaseUrl. Users with a versioned base path send requests to the wrong path.

## Location
- `Documentation~/Modules/Core.md:64`

## Problem
ResolveUri appends '/' to BaseUrl and calls new Uri(baseUri, url) (UHttpClient.cs:743-744), which follows RFC 3986 reference resolution: verified with new Uri(new Uri('https://example.com/api/'), '/users') = https://example.com/users and 'users' = https://example.com/api/users. Core.md:64 and APIReference.md:137 only say relative URLs are 'resolved against' BaseUrl, every example uses a leading slash with a host-only BaseUrl, and the one test covers 'users' (Tests/Runtime/Core/UHttpClientTests.Builders.cs:90-95).

**Failure scenario.** BaseUrl = 'https://api.example.com/v1' and client.Get('/users'), the pattern the docs teach: the request goes to https://api.example.com/users and returns 404.

## Spec reference
RFC 3986 section 5.2

## Suggested fix
Document both forms with a versioned BaseUrl example, add tests for the leading-slash case, or decide to treat BaseUrl as a prefix and say so.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Core.md and APIReference.md document both forms with a versioned BaseUrl example.
- [ ] A NUnit test in Tests/Runtime/Core/UHttpClientTests covers the leading-slash case against a BaseUrl with a path.
- [ ] If BaseUrl is instead changed to act as a prefix, the new behaviour is documented and tested.

title: [Docs] Docs say the request timeout 'covers each request' but a streaming response body has no deadline, and the examples do not bound body reads
body:
## Summary
For a streaming dispatch the HTTP/1.1 body source gets CancellationToken.None and the timeout source is disposed once headers arrive, so WithTimeout/DefaultTimeout does not bound body reads. Core.md says it covers each request, the streaming example passes a default token, and QuickStart and FileDownloader recommend streaming for large downloads. A stalled server hangs a download forever.

## Location
- `Documentation~/Modules/Core.md:130`

## Problem
Core.md:130: 'WithTimeout (or DefaultTimeout) covers each request'. For a streaming dispatch the HTTP/1.1 body source gets CancellationToken.None instead of the timeout token (RawSocketTransport.cs:1825-1829) and the timeout source is disposed when the dispatch returns at the headers (:439-441). The streaming example at Core.md:98-109 passes a ct declared as default, QuickStart.md:167 recommends streaming or FileDownloader for large downloads, FileDownloader streams (Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:399) with no stall bound, and Samples~/03-FileDownload/FileDownloadExample.cs:38 passes no token.

**Failure scenario.** Mobile network drops silently in the middle of a streamed download (half-open connection): Body.ReadAsync / FileDownloader.DownloadFileAsync never completes, the connection and its per-host permit stay held, and no Timeout error is raised.

## Suggested fix
State in Core.md and APIReference.md that the timeout ends when the response headers arrive for streaming responses, show a per-read or overall CancelAfter in the streaming and download examples, and consider an idle-read timeout option for streaming bodies.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Core.md and APIReference.md state that for streaming responses the timeout ends when headers arrive.
- [ ] Streaming and download examples show a per-read or overall CancelAfter.
- [ ] A decision is recorded on an idle-read timeout option for streaming bodies, filed as an issue if deferred.
- [ ] If behaviour changes, a test in Tests/Runtime/Transport/ shows a stalled body read is cancelled.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `docs-accuracy-08` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/docs.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: docs.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: DispatchCoreAsync creates the timeout source with 'using' (Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:439-441), and for a streaming dispatch the HTTP/1.1 body source gets CancellationToken.None instead of that token (:1825-1829). Http11ResponseBodySource uses the requestTimeout argument only for the error text (Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseBodySource.cs:63, :706-712). I looked for another bound and found none that covers a silent peer: StreamingOptions.Http2StallTimeoutSeconds covers a consumer that stops reading and blocked writes (Runtime/Core/StreamingOptions.cs:70-79), and SO_KEEPALIVE is enabled with OS default timing, about two hours (Runtime/Transport/Connection/HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:457-474). FileDownloader streams with only the caller's token (Runtime/Files/FileDownloader.cs:399) and the sample passes none (Samples~/03-FileDownload/FileDownloadExample.cs:38). Core.md:130 says the timeout 'covers each request'; no file in Documentation~ nor the DefaultTimeout/Timeout XML docs says it ends at the headers for streaming. No open issue tracks it.

title: [Docs] The record/replay example never disposes RecordReplayTransport or the RawSocketTransport it wraps
body:
## Summary
Testing.md creates a RecordReplayTransport around a RawSocketTransport, passes it to a client and says the recording flushes on Dispose. DisposeTransport defaults to false, so disposing the client does not dispose the transport and the flush and socket release never happen. Copying the example loses the recording and leaks sockets.

## Location

body:
## Summary
UniTask.md promises that continuations resume on the main thread and describes DefaultPlayerLoopTiming. AwaitResponse returns directly when the timing is Update, the default, so the continuation runs wherever the inner ValueTask resumed; only other timings yield to the player loop. The page also attributes the return to the main thread to UniTask's awaiter, omits the manual TURBOHTTP_UNITASK define needed when UniTask is not installed as the com.cysharp.unitask package, and the TurboHTTP.UniTask namespace makes a bare UniTask bind to the namespace in samples under TurboHTTP.*.

## Location
- `Documentation~/Modules/UniTask.md:11`

## Problem
:11 'Continuations resume on the main thread by UniTask's rules' and :33 on DefaultPlayerLoopTiming. AwaitResponse returns directly when the timing is Update, the default (Runtime/UniTask/UHttpClientUniTaskExtensions.cs:199-200, TurboHttpUniTaskOptions.cs:12), so the continuation runs wherever the inner ValueTask await resumed: the main thread only if the call started there with Unity's SynchronizationContext; any other timing does a UniTask.Yield onto the player loop. The XML doc calls the parameter the timing 'the result is delivered on' and the wrappers 'Zero-overhead'. :73 attributes the return to the main thread to 'UniTask's own awaiter'; it is the Task/ValueTask awaiter capturing the SynchronizationContext. :7 says the assemblies compile when the com.cysharp.unitask package is installed; a UniTask copied into Assets or shipped as a .unitypackage does not trigger the versionDefine and the manual TURBOHTTP_UNITASK define is not mentioned. The namespace TurboHTTP.UniTask also makes a bare UniTask bind to the namespace inside any TurboHTTP.* namespace (the package's own workaround: Runtime/UniTask.WebSocket/WebSocketUniTaskExtensions.cs:18-20), which hits users who extend the samples (namespace TurboHTTP.Samples.*).

**Failure scenario.** await UniTask.SwitchToThreadPool(); using var r = await client.GetAsync(url); texture.Apply(): with the default timing the continuation is on a thread-pool thread and the Unity call throws, although the docs promise the main thread.

## Suggested fix
Yield to the player loop when the completion is not on the main thread (or document the caller-context rule), correct the explanation, document the manual define, and avoid TurboHTTP.* namespaces in samples.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After await UniTask.SwitchToThreadPool(), awaiting a client call with the default timing resumes on the main thread, or the docs state the caller-context rule explicitly

title: [Unity] client.WebSocket(url) returns an already connected bridge and drops messages that arrive before OnMessage is subscribed
body:
## Summary
UnityWebSocketExtensions.WebSocket builds the bridge and awaits ConnectAsync before returning, and the bridge disposes any message that arrives while its own OnMessage has no handler. The documented snippet subscribes OnMessage after the await, so a message the server sends right after the handshake (greeting, auth challenge, snapshot) can be disposed without any warning. OnConnected can never be observed through this entry point either.

## Location
- `Documentation~/Modules/WebSocket.md:27`

## Problem
WebSocket.md:27-28: 'IWebSocketClient ws = await httpClient.WebSocket(url); ws.OnMessage += ...'. UnityWebSocketExtensions.WebSocket (Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketExtensions.cs:38-41) builds the bridge and awaits ConnectAsync before returning. The bridge subscribes the inner client's OnMessage in its constructor (UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:59), which puts the inner client in event mode, and HandleMessage disposes the message when the bridge's own OnMessage has no handler yet (UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:216-226). OnConnected can never be observed for the same reason. The example host echo.websocket.events sends a greeting as soon as the connection opens.

**Failure scenario.** Server sends a first message right after the handshake (auth challenge, snapshot, greeting). The await resumes on the main thread a frame later; the receive loop has already raised the message, the bridge found no handler and disposed it. The application never sees it and no drop event or warning is raised.

## Suggested fix
Offer an overload that takes handlers or a configure callback before connecting (or return an unconnected bridge), or buffer messages in the bridge until the first OnMessage subscription; document the ordering in WebSocket.md.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Messages that arrive between connect and the first OnMessage subscription are delivered, or an overload lets the caller attach handlers before connecting
- [ ] OnConnected is observable through client.WebSocket(url), or the API documents that it is not
- [ ] WebSocket.md documents the subscription ordering
- [ ] Regression test in Tests/Runtime/Unity/ with a server that sends a frame immediately after the handshake and a subscriber attached after the await; fails before the fix

Verifier note: client.WebSocket(uri) constructs the bridge and awaits ConnectAsync before returning (Runtime/Unity.WebSocket/UnityWebSocketExtensions.cs:38-41). The bridge subscribes the inner OnMessage in its constructor (UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:59), so the inner listener takes the event path for every message (Runtime/WebSocket/WebSocketClient.cs:409-431), and HandleMessage disposes the event copy when the bridge's own OnMessage has no handler (UnityWebSocketBridge.cs:216-226). title: [Docs] JSON helpers (GetJsonAsync, PostJsonAsync, PutJsonAsync, PatchJsonAsync, DeleteJsonAsync) throw on non-2xx but docs and samples do not say so
body:
## Summary
Every JSON extension helper calls EnsureSuccessStatusCode and disposes the response, so a 404 or 422 with a JSON error body throws UHttpException and the body is lost. README, QuickStart and APIReference present the helpers next to the statement that 4xx/5xx are normal responses without noting this. QuickStart and the JsonApi sample call them from async void without try/catch, and QuickStart uses TryAsJson without checking the status.

## Location
- `Documentation~/QuickStart.md:137`

## Problem
Each helper calls response.EnsureSuccessStatusCode() and disposes the response (Runtime/JSON/JsonExtensions.cs:88-96, 109-118, 132-141, 155-164, 176-185), so the error body is lost and UHttpError carries only the status. README.md:123 and :141, QuickStart.md:58 and :113-148, APIReference.md:173-180 present the helpers next to 'HTTP 4xx/5xx are normal responses, not exceptions' with no note. QuickStart.md:137 and Samples~/02-JsonApi/JsonApiExample.cs:47-54 call them from async void without try/catch. QuickStart.md:142 uses TryAsJson without checking the status, which with JsonUtility returns true and a default-valued object for a JSON error body.

**Failure scenario.** The API answers 404 or 422 with a JSON problem document: GetJsonAsync throws UHttpException (HttpError) out of async void Start as an unhandled exception, and the caller cannot read the server's error payload.

## Suggested fix
Document the throw in APIReference.md and QuickStart.md (and in the XML summary of the README sentence), wrap the QuickStart and sample calls in try/catch, and check IsSuccessStatusCode before TryAsJson; consider carrying the error body on the exception.

title: [Docs] Samples and QuickStart run requests from async void without try/catch or cancellation and dispose the client mid-flight
body:
## Summary
Samples 01, 02, 04, 05 and QuickStart call requests from async void with no try/catch, so a network failure surfaces as an unhandled exception and later examples never run. OnDestroy disposes the client without cancelling pending work, and sample 05 sets DisposeInterceptors = true so the cache and limiter are disposed under concurrent requests. Sample 03 claims resume support but downloads an endpoint without validators.

## Location
- `Samples~/01-BasicUsage/BasicUsageExample.cs:42`

## Problem
RunExamples is async void with no try/catch in samples 01 (:42-50), 02 (:47-54), 04 (:39-43) and 05 (:70-77); only one example per sample catches UHttpException. They call httpbin.org and jsonplaceholder.typicode.com. OnDestroy disposes the client with no token to cancel pending work; sample 05 sets DisposeInterceptors = true (:36), so the cache and limiter are disposed under the six concurrent requests of Example3. QuickStart.md:98-107 and :135-144 do the same. Both specialist rubrics list 'avoid async void' and cancellation propagation. Sample 03 names resume support but downloads httpbin /bytes, which sends no validator, so resume is never exercised.

**Failure scenario.** No network or httpbin down: the first failing await throws out of async void, Unity logs an unhandled exception and the remaining examples never run. Stopping play mode mid-run leaves requests running and, in sample 05, failing against disposed interceptors.

## Suggested fix
Wrap each sample run in one try/catch for UHttpException and OperationCanceledException, create a CancellationTokenSource cancelled in OnDestroy and pass it to every send, and use a resumable URL in the download sample.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each sample run is wrapped in try/catch for UHttpException and OperationCanceledException.
- [ ] A CancellationTokenSource cancelled in OnDestroy is passed to every send.
- [ ] The download sample uses a URL that supports resume (validator and ranges).

title: [Auth] AuthInterceptor sends the token to every origin a client is used for; sample claims it never goes to another host and docs give no warning
body:
## Summary
AuthInterceptor binds the origin per call, so the first hop of every request always receives the token and only redirect hops are filtered. The Authentication sample comment says the token is never sent to another host, and Auth.md has no warning about using the same client for other hosts. A client with a BaseUrl and AuthInterceptor used for a third-party URL sends Authorization: Bearer to that host.

## Location
- `Samples~/04-Authentication/AuthenticationExample.cs:12`

## Problem
The sample comment (:12-13) says the interceptor 'keeps the token bound to the origin it was first used with, so it is never sent to another host'. AuthInterceptor.IsBoundOrigin binds per RequestContext, that is per call: the first hop of every request is always the bound origin (Runtime/Auth/AuthInterceptor.cs:112-129), so only redirect hops are protected. There is no allowed-origin option. Auth.md:18 words it correctly ('for each call') but gives no guidance for requests to other hosts through the same client.

**Failure scenario.** A client with BaseUrl https://api.game.com and AuthInterceptor is also used for client.GetTextureAsync('https://cdn.thirdparty.net/a.png') or a user-supplied URL: the request carries Authorization: Bearer <api token> to the third party.

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 section 11.6.2

## Suggested fix
Correct the sample comment, add a warning to Auth.md to use a dedicated client per authenticated origin, and consider an optional origin allow-list on AuthInterceptor so the non-negotiable 'credentials stay with their origin' is enforceable.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Samples~/04-Authentication comment is corrected and Auth.md warns to use a dedicated client per authenticated origin.
- [ ] AuthInterceptor offers an optional origin allow-list; a request to a host outside it carries no Authorization header.
- [ ] NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Auth/ that fails before the fix: a request to a non-allowed origin through the same client has no Authorization header.

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `docs-accuracy-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/docs.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: IsBoundOrigin stores the first request Uri in RequestContext state and compares later hops against it (Runtime/Auth/AuthInterceptor.cs:112-129). Each send creates a new RequestContext (Runtime/Core/UHttpClient.cs:395), so the first hop of every call is the bound origin and gets the token; only redirect hops are filtered. There is no origin allow-list. The class XML doc (AuthInterceptor.cs:13-20) and Auth.md:18 ('for each call') describe this correctly; the sample comment at Samples~/04-Authentication/AuthenticationExample.cs:12-13 ('bound to the origin it was first used with, so it is never sent to another host') does not, and neither Auth.md nor Interceptors.md warns against using an authenticated client for other hosts. This is conventional behaviour for an auth interceptor, so the defect is the sample's claim plus the missing guidance; the token does go to any host a shared client is used for, which the project's own 'Authorization stays with its origin' rule forbids.

Related: [[R11-docs-accuracy-27]].

title: [Docs] Authentication sample token provider is not thread-safe, ignores its CancellationToken and logs the bearer token
body:
## Summary
DynamicTokenProvider keeps its cached token in a plain field accessed from thread-pool threads and the main thread, has no single-flight refresh and ignores the CancellationToken. The sample also logs the httpbin /bearer response body, which echoes the token. Projects copying it refresh in parallel and leak tokens into device logs; the shipped OAuthTokenProvider is not shown.

## Location
- `Samples~/04-Authentication/AuthenticationExample.cs:99`

## Problem
DynamicTokenProvider keeps _cachedToken in a plain field read and written by GetTokenAsync (:99-106), which AuthInterceptor calls on thread-pool threads with ConfigureAwait(false) (Runtime/Auth/AuthInterceptor.cs:66), and by InvalidateToken from the main thread (:108-111); there is no single-flight, and the cancellationToken parameter is unused. :54 logs GetBodyAsString() of httpbin /bearer, whose JSON contains the token. The library ships OAuthTokenProvider with per-key refresh gates (Runtime/Auth/OAuthClient.cs:163-166) that the sample does not show.

**Failure scenario.** A project copies DynamicTokenProvider: ten parallel requests after expiry each call the token endpoint, a refresh cannot be cancelled when the request is, and tokens appear in device logs once the pattern is used with a real API.

## Suggested fix
Guard the refresh with a SemaphoreSlim and Volatile reads, pass the token through, drop the body log (or redact it), and point to OAuthTokenProvider.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The sample guards refresh with a SemaphoreSlim and Volatile reads and honours the CancellationToken.
- [ ] The sample no longer logs the token-bearing body and points to OAuthTokenProvider.

PRELUDE adds System.Collections.Generic and System.IO (:30-31) to fragments, while APIReference.md:5 and Core.md:5 tell readers the assumed header is System, System.Threading, System.Threading.Tasks, UnityEngine, TurboHTTP.Core; a fragment using List<T>, Dictionary or Path would pass CI and not compile for a reader. APIReference.md:3 says 'Every C# snippet in this documentation is compiled'; doc_snippets.py reports 67 blocks, 61 compiled, 6 skipped (APIReference.md:211, MigrationGuide.md:12 and :43, UniTask.md:15, :41, :58). The three UniTask snippets are skipped although the shadow build has UniTask whenever --no-unitask is not passed. Nothing executes a snippet, which is how the always-throwing plugin example (docs-accuracy-03) passes; test_doc_snippets.py covers only extraction and rendering.

**Failure scenario.** A UniTask adapter is renamed: the adapters and their tests are updated, UniTask.md keeps the old name and CI stays green. A future fragment that needs System.Collections.Generic compiles in CI and fails when pasted under the documented header.

## Suggested fix
Align PRELUDE with the documented header (or the header with PRELUDE), compile the UniTask snippets when UniTask is present, reword the claim, and run at least the declaration snippets that need no network in a smoke test.
